## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Brahmālittheragāthā* (Thag 2.43) is a short poetic discourse situated within the *Dukanipāta* of the *Theragāthā* in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. It records the verses attributed to the elder Brahmāli [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into eight modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato hosted on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Regarding textual parallels and reuse, automated analysis by DharmaNexus identifies no significant Pali-internal reuse or cross-language alignments with a match score of ten or greater [DharmaNexus]. However, curated parallels on SuttaCentral record multiple resembling passages across Buddhist canonical literature [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali tradition, its verses resemble *Dhammapada* verse 94 (Dhp 94) [SuttaCentral]. Further resembling verses are found across northern and Indic transmission lineages, notably in the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 84–95, *Śokavagga*), the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 19 / UVS 19, *Aśvavarga*), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 19), and several Chinese translations including the *Faju jing* (T 210.15, T 210.31), the *Chu yao jing* (T 212.20), and the *Fa ji yao song jing* (T 213.19) [SuttaCentral].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
